subject: HealthCore evaluation — MAP, acceptance criteria, and close timeline
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Sharma <maya@healthcore.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HealthCore evaluation — MAP, acceptance criteria, and close timeline

Maya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great questions from the ML and platform teams. Per our conversation, I put together a one-page Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft that aligns on success metrics, exit gates, and a proposed close timeline so your procurement and security teams can start parallel reviews. High-level items in the attached spreadsheet:

- Week 0: Kickoff & environment access (sandbox credentials, IP allowlist)
- Week 1–2: Integration & baseline performance runs (latency/throughput)
- Week 3: Acceptance tests (functional prompts, latency SLAs, stability run)
- Week 4: Security/compliance evidence + contract redlines
- Week 5: Go/no-go and recommended production cutover window

Key acceptance criteria (draft):
- Quality: pass rate >= 90% on curated prompt set (see acceptance-tests-compact.md)
- Latency: 95th percentile response <= 350ms for 1K token requests in sandbox
- Reliability: no more than 1% error rate during a 24-hour stability run
- Data controls: VPC peering and audit-log delivery validated

Attached: HealthCore_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP + timeline), acceptance-tests-compact.md (sample prompts & pass/fail), SLA-summary.pdf (baseline SLA we typically target).

Can you confirm the internal reviewers and any procurement windows we should be aware of? If that looks good, we’ll convert the MAP to a shared Google doc and start the acceptance-test run as soon as we get sandbox creds.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0128

Attachment: HealthCore_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: acceptance-tests-compact.md (text)
Attachment: SLA-summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Maya Sharma <maya@healthcore.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Liu <ben.liu@healthcore.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthCore evaluation — MAP, acceptance criteria, and close timeline

Karthik —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. MAP looks sensible. A few notes from our side:

- Reviewers: Security (Maya), ML bench (Ben), Procurement (Sara Lee - cc'd separately in our system).
- Procurement window: our quarter close is 10/29; we’d prefer to sign prior to that but can extend to 11/05 in exceptional cases.
- Sandbox access: Ben will request service account + IP ranges today. Expect creds by EOD Monday (10/5).

Acceptance test tweaks:
- Add one synthetic spike test to validate autoscaling behavior under burst (2–5x baseline).
- For quality we care about hallucination on a specific protected entity set — I’ll share a short list tomorrow.

Agree on timeline otherwise. Can you add a short success rubric for security evidence (SOC2 evidence, log export examples) so our auditor has something to track?

Appreciate it —
Maya
Maya Sharma
Head of Security, HealthCore Analytics
maya@healthcore.com

Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthCore evaluation — MAP, acceptance criteria, and close timeline

Maya, Ben —

Appreciate the clarity on reviewers and timeline. I updated the MAP and attached a compact acceptance-tests.md that includes:

- Functional prompt set (30 prompts + expected signals)
- Autoscale spike scenario steps and expected behavior
- Hallucination probes for protected entities (please send your list and we’ll incorporate)
- Test run pass/fail thresholds and reporting template

Security rubric (high level) — included in SLA-summary.pdf and summarized below so procurement has a checklist:
- SOC2: we’ll provide our SOC2 Type II report and the mapping table for controls relevant to inference (delivered via secure link).
- Audit logs: sample log exports and field dictionary (will run during sandbox tests).
- Key management: KMS integration tested in sandbox; HSM options available in Private offering.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben sends sandbox creds and IPs (ETA 10/5 EOD)
2) Redwood runs baseline perf + functional test (we’ll share a report within 48 hours)
3) HealthCore runs targeted hallucination probe and autoscale spike (your side)
4) Joint stability run (24 hours)
5) Security evidence handoff + procurement redlines

If that sequence works I’ll convert the MAP to a shared Google Doc and lock in dates on the calendar.

-Karthik

Attachment: HealthCore_MAP_v1.xlsx (updated)
Attachment: acceptance-tests-compact.md (updated)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: HealthCore MAP — SLA callouts and discount ask

Karthik / Monica —

Quick internal note before we go live with the shared doc: procurement is likely to push on two areas — a 12‑month minimum term and a discount tied to committed volume. If we want to keep the deal within our standard T&Cs and still land this before their procurement window (10/29), recommend:

- Offer: 6-month initial term + opt-in 12-month auto-renewal after successful pilot.
- Commercial concession: 10% first‑year volume discount if they commit to > $200k ARR.
- SLA fallback: automatic fallback to smaller model variant and rate limit policy during overload (call this out in the MAP).

Also, we should confirm we can deliver the SOC2 artifacts within 3 business days of request — legal already approved share via secure link, but ops needs to be ready to run the sample export. Monica, can you confirm ops can run a sample export on short notice?

- Rachel
Rachel Kim
Director, Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: HealthCore evaluation — MAP, acceptance criteria, and close timeline

Maya / Ben —

Thanks — Ben confirmed sandbox creds delivered (service account + IP allowlist). We kicked off the baseline perf tests this morning and will share the first pass report by Friday. A few clarifications after internal review (copied Rachel / Monica):

- Hallucination probe: please send the protected-entity list (csv) by EOD tomorrow so we can add it to the functional set.
- Spike test: Redwood will run the controlled 3x spike (5 minutes) and provide telemetry; HealthCore should mirror on your side per test script so we get a 2-sided comparison.
- Contract: we’ll start with the 6-month pilot term + proposed commercial concession (10% first‑year discount at >$200k ARR) — Karthik to get final sign-off from Pricing.
- Security evidence: Monica confirmed ops can run a sample audit-log export within 2 business days once they approve a secure link; Rachel, legal will push docs to the secure share today.

Next actions summary:
- HealthCore (Ben): confirm protected-entity CSV and run local side of spike test (ETA 10/8)
- Redwood (Karthik/ops): deliver baseline perf report and run 24-hr stability after joint tests (report ETA 10/9)
- Procurement (HealthCore): target decision by 10/29; alternate cutoff 11/05

If all goes well we’ll convert the MAP to a final signoff doc and circulate a DocuSign link for the pilot SOW.

Best,
Karthik
